note: Misses on all five criteria as written, and the rep spent 102 minutes and two financing links on him anyway. Occupation is an outside sales rep for a linen rental company on flat commission with no base, actively job-hunting — not a business owner, physician or equivalent. Income is $65-70k with two months of zero sales earlier in the year, and he said it himself: 'Maybe he's used to dealing with people that make more money than me. I don't make six figures.' Health is not the neglected area but an active crisis — severe fatty liver with scarring, sleep apnoea, blood pressure problems, bilateral irreparable rotator cuff tears and a stated belief that inaction ends in a heart attack. This is rescue, not good-to-great: he is 45-50 lb above his own target by his own count and doing no strength training at all. The exclusion criterion half-applies and is worth reading carefully — he is at roughly the 50 lb overweight threshold the quote names, but he is the precise opposite of gym-averse, having trained in martial arts since 1978 and served in the Marine Corps. That split is the finding: the stated ICP bundles body composition and attitude into one test, and this prospect fails one half while being the most motivated person in the batch. He is also the counterpart to the recorded observation that the buying population is wider than the stated ICP — here an outside-ICP prospect did not close, and the reason was income, exactly the criterion the ICP screens on.
